source.title: The Self-Improvement Paradox: Can Language Models Bootstrap Reasoning Capabilities without External Scaffolding?
source.authors: Yu-Tao Sun; Ming-Shuai Chen; Tiancheng Zhao; Ruochen Xu; Zilun Zhang; Jianwei Yin

record.tranche_reason: The study varies the amount of synthetic SFT data and measures downstream accuracy, extending downstream scaling questions to a self-generated-data fine-tuning setting. It does not reproduce pretraining loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al.'s scaling laws as background but does not test their loss, parameter-count, token-count, or compute relationships. Its synthetic-data-volume sweep bears on V6 by measuring downstream accuracy at different training-data volumes. Other benchmark comparisons concern self-improvement, not the scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Kaplan et al. only as background. Its one sweep varies synthetic SFT data volume (25k–150k) for a single 8B model and reports GSM8K accuracy qualitatively from a figure. There is no pretraining loss, no parameter, token or compute scaling, and no power-law fit. Downstream gains from a fine-tuning data-volume sweep are a related but different construct from V6 (predictability with model or pretraining scale, or with loss). Without any functional fit they also do not bear on V5's power-law form for fine-tuning.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that CRESCENT's fully self-generated QA data improves math reasoning without external supervision while preserving general capabilities, and distils knowledge to weaker models better than seed-based methods. They also report that data-volume gains plateau beyond 75k.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tunes an instruction-tuned model on self-generated synthetic QA data and evaluates downstream accuracy; it does not fit pretraining-loss scaling laws or sweep parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Synthetic-data volume: reported improvements from 25k to 75k stabilize between 75k and 150k.

fits_no_version.finding: One-epoch SFT of Llama3-8B-Instruct on self-generated math QA: GSM8K accuracy improves from 25k to 75k examples, then plateaus up to 150k (Fig. 7, qualitative only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream accuracy gains from fine-tuning on self-generated synthetic data saturate with data volume, rather than following a power law.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: Figure 7 values are not given numerically in the text; the trend is reported qualitatively. The scaling analysis covers one model, one synthetic-data SFT setup, and GSM8K accuracy, not pretraining loss or model-size/compute scaling.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss or parameter, token or compute scaling.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No power-law fit for fine-tuning or other regimes. The SFT data sweep is qualitative only.
No downstream performance versus model scale or pretraining loss.
No fitted exponents or comparison of fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T3 and its V6 labels are withdrawn. V6 concerns scale or pretraining-loss predictability, whereas this study is a self-improvement method paper with a small, unfitted SFT data-volume sweep reported only in a figure.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy or parameter, token, or compute scaling.
No extrapolation from smaller runs to larger runs.
No comparison of depth, width, or architecture at fixed parameter count.
No tests of scaling laws across modalities or the listed alternative training regimes.
Tests downstream math accuracy against synthetic SFT data volume only; it does not test prediction from pretraining loss or model-scale sweeps.
No fitted scaling exponents or comparison of fitting choices.
